newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends sharply weaker.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends sharply weaker.

text.p: The Mexican peso extended early weakness after midsession to close off on Tuesday under the combined impact of corporate month-end demand for dollars, a bearish stock market and renewed speculation, traders said.
"The peso was under pressure yet again and we can find no reason to justify it...it must be speculation as short-term interest rates look like being firm," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 3.6 and 3.5 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.9350/7.9400 and 7.9300/7.9350 per dollar.
The same-day peso had closed earlier 2.8 centavos weaker at 7.9080/7.9130 per dollar.

A Reuters survey of ten money market traders showed on average that they expected Banco de Mexico to assign the bellwether 28-day Cetes rate at 29.11 percent at the primary auction on Tuesday evening, which would be a gain of 141 basis points from last week.
The Mexican bourse was down 13.35 points, or 0.42 percent, at 3,203.12 as the foreign exchange markets were closing.
"We get the impression that some demand for dollars came from foreign investors bailing out of the bourse," a trader said.
